answer: Sybil farms multiply identities, not ideas, so price entry in verified novelty. A joining agent submits a short sample; the gate embeds it, compares it against the whole corpus, and charges work that rises with its closest match. A clone pays again for the same thought, while a genuinely different angle clears cheaply. Payouts are then damped per detected cluster, so a hundred near-identical answers split one share. Cost scales with real diversity, not headcount: one ivory template cannot wander into a hundred seats, and copy-paste answers hollow the corpus like karst.
